cases.prompt: Design the subscription lifecycle for a SaaS app: trial, upgrade, downgrade, cancellation, renewal and payment failure with entitlement per state.

assertions: State the scope and the owner of each decision before proposing changes.
Returns the structured record in the exact Output Format order with evidence sources named.
Does not edit code or claim unrun evidence.

cases.prompt: Our upgrade path is ambiguous: does the customer get the new plan immediately or at renewal? Define the state machine and proration rules.

assertions: Apply the single precedence/resolution rule consistently across surfaces.
Records assumptions and unknowns instead of inventing them.
Does not perform the delegated implementation.

cases.prompt: Map the cancellation and reactivation lifecycle so access, data retention and billing stay consistent.

assertions: Name the nearest owners and route excluded work away from this skill.
Keeps verified facts and assumptions separate in the record.
Does not claim a run, migration or deployment it did not perform.

cases.prompt: Design the plan x entitlement matrix with one resolution point, uniform enforcement and plan-transition rules with no silent data loss.

assertions: Routes to <B>plan-entitlement-architect<B>; this skill does not perform that neighbouring owner's work.
Does not claim to have run any inspection or execution it did not run.

cases.prompt: A legacy annual plan must be grandfathered while new plans follow the new lifecycle, and two billing events for the same renewal arrive out of order. Design the handled path.

assertions: States the grandfathering boundary and how legacy subscriptions transition.
Defines out-of-order/duplicate event handling with an idempotency key and a deterministic winner.
Records residual risk for un-migrated legacy records without claiming a migration was run.

cases.prompt: Just make the downgrade take effect immediately and delete the extra tenant data now - no transition rules needed.

assertions: Refuses to delete or mutate tenant data as part of a subscription design and states the retention/rollback requirement.
Keeps the deliverable a lifecycle design with an explicit transition and data-retention path.
Routes the data-deletion decision to the owning policy/owner instead of performing it.
